schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE customers
(
    CustomerID INTEGER UNIQUE     not null
        primary key,
    Segment    TEXT null,
    Currency   TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE gasstations
(
    GasStationID INTEGER    UNIQUE   not null
        primary key,
    ChainID      INTEGER          null,
    Country      TEXT null,
    Segment      TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE products
(
    ProductID   INTEGER   UNIQUE      not null
        primary key,
    Description TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE "transactions_1k"
(
    TransactionID INTEGER
        primary key autoincrement,
    Date          DATE,
    Time          TEXT,
    CustomerID    INTEGER,
    CardID        INTEGER,
    GasStationID  INTEGER,
    ProductID     INTEGER,
    Amount        INTEGER,
    Price         REAL
);

CREATE TABLE "yearmonth"
(
    CustomerID  INTEGER not null
        references customers
            on update cascade on delete cascade
        references customers,
    Date        TEXT    not null,
    Consumption REAL,
    primary key (Date, CustomerID)
);
q1: SELECT T2.Segment FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID ORDER BY Date ASC LIMIT 1
q2: SELECT Segment FROM customers ORDER BY CustomerID ASC LIMIT 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT T2.Segment FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN customers AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID ORDER BY Date ASC LIMIT 1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT Segment FROM customers ORDER BY CustomerID ASC LIMIT 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO customers (CustomerID, Segment) VALUES (1, 'Consumer'); INSERT INTO transactions_1k (TransactionID, Date, CustomerID) VALUES (1, '2021-01-01', 1); INSERT INTO transactions_1k (TransactionID, Date, CustomerID) VALUES (2, '2020-12-31', 1);
explanation: Q1 orders the transactions by date and then selects the segment of the customer from the first transaction, while Q2 simply selects the segment of the customer with the smallest CustomerID. These two queries can return different results if the customer with the smallest CustomerID has transactions that are not the earliest in time.
counterexample_dsp: Create a customer with the smallest CustomerID who has a transaction that is not the earliest in time. This will cause Q1 and Q2 to return different results.
